items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And then when I moved to Manhattan I studied with Orin O’Brien, who is a lady bassist in the philharmonic.

ctx.x: You must have got significant classical training in the conservatory?

I did. I didn’t stay in the conservatory that long, but when I first started playing the bass I was thumping around on it, and thinking I was getting pretty good. My father brought home a bow, and he said, “Here, try it with this.” And it was so depressing when he did it. I didn’t touch the bass for about two weeks, and I really thought, do I really want to do this? And he said, “Well if you’re going to play the thing, you ought to learn how to play it right.” And I started with the principal bassist in the…
What is it about his playing that’s kept you two together for so many years?
